prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

You are reviewing layouts of one table, all rendered in a real browser with identical content, font, padding and colours; only column widths differ. You do not know who or what produced them. The first image is the content overview (every cell on one line).
Table: Lange deutsche Komposita (language de).
Grid: 3 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "Begriff" · longest unbreakable word 546px · one-line width 546px
  col 2: header "Kurzform" · longest unbreakable word 83px · one-line width 101px
  col 3: header "Erklärung" · longest unbreakable word 186px · one-line width 1091px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 360px (the dashed pink box = the reader's viewport). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 359px.
This table cannot fit without splitting words at 360px. You MAY choose a total wider than 359px (the reader then scrolls horizontally), or squeeze and accept splits — a design decision.
Rendering convention: the screenshot always shows the WHOLE table. Anything beyond the dashed box is not clipped; it is the part a reader reaches by scrolling sideways, so judge both what fits in the box at first sight and the cost of scrolling to the rest.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

Rate EACH layout independently: "excellent" | "good" | "acceptable" | "poor" | "bad", with a short reason that points at what you see. Then name the best layout(s) (ties allowed), say how confident you are (low/medium/high), and note anything you are unsure about.
Reply ONLY JSON: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"","why":""},"B":{"grade":"","why":""},"C":{"grade":"","why":""},"D":{"grade":"","why":""},"E":{"grade":"","why":""},"F":{"grade":"","why":""}},"best":["letter"],"confidence":"","unsure":""}

log.raw: {"ratings":{"A":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"The wider Begriff column keeps the long compounds in relatively few fragments, and the abbreviations are easy to scan. Almost all of Erklärung lies beyond the initial viewport, so reading across each row requires scrolling."},"B":{"grade":"poor","why":"All three columns fit in the viewport, but the narrow Begriff and Erklärung columns break many words into small fragments. The resulting tall rows make both reading and comparison laborious."},"C":{"grade":"poor","why":"The first column preserves more of the long terms, but it occupies the whole initial viewport and extends beyond it. The abbreviations and explanations require substantial horizontal scrolling, while large blank areas weaken the row rhythm."},"D":{"grade":"good","why":"Begriff and Kurzform are visible together, and the compounds generally occupy two or three lines. Erklärung starts within the viewport, although reading it still requires horizontal scrolling and several words are split."},"E":{"grade":"good","why":"The three headers and the start of each explanation appear in the viewport. Begriff remains reasonably readable, though the longest term ends with an isolated letter and the explanations require scrolling."},"F":{"grade":"acceptable","why":"The three columns begin within the viewport, but the narrower Begriff column breaks terms more often and the explanation column produces tall rows with frequent word splits. Scrolling is still needed to read the explanations."}},"best":["D","E"],"confidence":"medium","unsure":"The supplied views cut off the right side of the wider layouts, so the full explanation widths and total scrolling distance are difficult to judge precisely. D gives the terms more room; E reveals slightly more of the explanations initially."}
